exposition_seal.compressed_statement: For Borel measurable odd U:R->R satisfying |U(y)|<=beta|y| for every y, fixed a in [0,1], and centered Gaussian law N(0,v) with v>=0, exp(-aU) is integrable and its integral is at most exp(beta^2*v/2). beta>=0 is derived; v=0 is included.
exposition_seal.reader_default_view: Attributed complete statement and assumptions, three formula-led moves, exact initially folded Lean statement/proof with step-level Lean explanations, and the explicit generalized-only boundary. The authored progressive lesson is unchanged from exact980 reader QA.

lossless_expansion.title: Establish an integrable envelope first
lossless_expansion.source_role: Discharge the source's omitted analytic prerequisite, not add an integrability binder.
lossless_expansion.formula: |aU(y)|<=|beta*y|; exp(+-aU(y))<=exp(|beta*y|)<=exp(beta*y)+exp(-beta*y). Measurable composition and the two integrable Gaussian exponential terms prove both signs integrable.

lossless_expansion.title: Use symmetry to average the two exponential signs
lossless_expansion.formula: Centered reflection and oddness give integral exp(aU)=integral exp(-aU); the already integrable pair can be averaged, yielding integral exp(-aU)=integral cosh(aU). This holds also for Dirac zero.

lossless_expansion.title: Compare with the linear Gaussian load
lossless_expansion.formula: cosh(aU(y))<=cosh(beta*y) by absolute arguments, not global monotonicity on R. The two signed Gaussian MGF values average to exp(beta^2*v/2), with no factor 2 loss.
